purpose: Active multiview collaboration contract. Structural checks only; business confirmation, compatibility and independent semantic acceptance remain distinct. Old artifacts keep their original schema.

artifact_locations.note: These are run-workspace process artifacts, not platform storage. A missing, non-JSON, symlinked, or escaping path is rejected without touching anything outside the run directory.

rules: Top-level fields are closed: schema_version, scenario_id, topology_decision_ref and the six required_sections. Contract metadata is never an artifact field.
Each slice has exactly slices_item_fields. All fields except viewpoints are nonempty strings; slice_id is unique.
Shared definitions are registered by definition_id, not term; one owner_slice resolves to a known slice. used_by_slices is nonempty and contains known slices.
Use the closed viewpoints, shared_terms and adjustments contracts above. Candidate/item identities are neutral; revision is a positive integer, not a boolean.
Dependencies, cross-slice questions, explicit_unknowns and topology_decision_ref retain the r3-0-002 field contracts, enumerated below so this mounted contract is self-contained.
Ordinary adjustments use only change and approved_by_coordinator (nonempty strings). Shared meaning changes also carry review.
Errors identify item/field locations and can be corrected within the same run; no view count, reviewer count or semantic compatibility gate is added.
An array, possibly empty; no repeated viewpoint per slice; note is nonempty.
Absent viewpoints are unassessed, never implicitly not_applicable. No mandatory seven-phase sequence or one Agent per viewpoint.
Partial expression takes modeled with remaining work/unknowns in note. An expression that correctly preserves necessary unknowns may also be modeled; it does not confirm those facts.

Judge current content, not monotonic status upgrades: when a revision invalidates expression, retain only still-valid scope and identify old references as historical. slices[].status remains a textual overview, not a state machine or percentage.

Note locates the current complete immutable candidate_id/revision/key item_id or approved path, explains analyzed/expressed scope, remaining work/unknowns and next responsible role/input. Note references are semantically checked by Coordinator, not a new structured field or regex gate.

status_meanings.pending: Registered but no locatable current model expression, including work needing redo. Explain completed analysis, remaining work and next step; do not hide existing partial expression.
status_meanings.modeled: A locatable current model expression exists within approved scope, possibly only part of the viewpoint. Explain current candidate/revision/items, expressed scope, remaining work and unknowns. This is not full completion, business confirmation, application, acceptance PASS or write permission.
status_meanings.unknown: No confirmable current expression and progress depends on unresolved business facts or conflicts. Explain the question, affected scope and required respondent/input; work not yet analyzed alone is pending.
status_meanings.not_applicable: Business grounds establish that this viewpoint does not apply within the approved slice scope. State scope and reason; missing material or artifacts alone is insufficient.

note_example.note: Expressed: main and fallback flow, candidate-flow revision 3 / flow-main, flow-fallback. Remaining: compensation path; unknown: compensation trigger needs business-owner confirmation. Next: Modeling revises after confirmation; Coordinator updates progress. Candidate not applied. Syntax illustration only, not business evidence.

rules: definition_id is a stable neutral semantic key, not an IRI; it is unique within the scenario/authorized Project. Same term with different meaning_scope may have distinct keys. Do not merge unconfirmed synonyms.
owner_slice resolves to slices[].owner; maintenance ownership grants no semantic access.
candidate_refs may be empty before publication; otherwise each points to an item in a complete immutable unified candidate at its current revision.
Same definition across candidates reuses the approved read/receipt-bound platform identity; never create a synonymous duplicate. confirmed means business confirmation only.

definition_ids references the registered shared keys. before_refs and after_refs use candidate_ref_fields; before_refs are historical, after_refs current. For a new definition before_refs can be empty; obtain an authorized baseline before changing existing meaning.

References resolve to checked candidate items within slice scope; revised references point to the after revision. notes explain impact and old location. Other results point to the checked current revision.

coverage concerns only the declared authorized scope. Record direct and known indirect dependencies in processes, rules, parameters, mappings and public CQs. Truncation, expired reads, unlocated external consumers or unresolved dependencies mean incomplete, never no references.

outcome and approval of this record do not authorize apply. Keep candidate unknowns/conflicting_meanings; delay only unsafe changes. Actual application still requires content-bound business and translation approval.

identity_rules: schema_version is exactly r4-0-007-scenario-map/v1; scenario_id is a nonempty string.

topology_decision_ref is a string: empty/whitespace while undecided, otherwise its trimmed value is exactly topology-decision.json. Recording a reference does not create or approve the topology artifact.
All six required_sections are arrays; slices has at least one item, while the other five arrays may be empty. The three inherited sections below are top-level arrays, never fields inside slices[].

rules: Each item is an object with exactly these fields. from_slice and to_slice are existing slices[].slice_id values.
direction is a nonempty string, with no structural enum. connection_points is a nonempty array of nonempty strings.
Record actual dependencies from authorized inputs and explain their direction; example values illustrate syntax only and prescribe no business dependency.
Each item is an object with exactly these fields. question_id and question are nonempty strings.

spans_slices describes at least two distinct actual slices, each an existing slices[].slice_id value. Never repeat a slice ID to simulate cross-slice scope. With only one actual slice use an empty cross_slice_competency_questions list, including for panorama public questions.
Use authorized public questions only; this section is not approval and must not contain hidden acceptance questions or expected answers.
Each item is an object with exactly these fields; all three values are nonempty strings. status has no structural enum.
Record actual unresolved topics and who or what is needed to resolve them; do not invent missing business facts.

scenario_map.syntax_example_note: This complete mechanically valid example uses neutral placeholders solely to show field shapes. It supplies no business facts, CQ answers, semantic confirmation, approval or topology choice; author the actual artifact from authorized inputs. Metadata keys such as identity_rules, fields, rules and syntax_example are not artifact fields.

cross_slice_competency_questions.question: Placeholder authorized question spanning the declared scopes?

progress_maintenance.owner: Coordinator alone authors the shared map. Modeling sends coverage and candidate locations through existing handoff/revision messages; Protocol sends bound execution-result summaries without reading the private map.
progress_maintenance.when: Check accessible actual candidate content at candidate handoff, content-affecting revision, before planned handoff/save and after recovery before the next step. Before production terminal, synchronize the map, then bind it through existing handoff digest. Normal order: final facts checked, Coordinator synchronizes and reports production terminal, then host verifies quiescence/write draining and publishes the existing digest-bound handoff; Coordinator never publishes that host handoff.
progress_maintenance.evidence: Oral completion, file existence, item count and structure PASS do not prove expression. If actual content cannot be checked, explicitly retain an unverified note and request the missing artifact. Ordinary stale progress is recoverable feedback, never an all-modeled or view-count gate.
progress_maintenance.related_records: Retain real business unknowns consistently in explicit_unknowns and necessary candidate unknowns/conflicting_meanings. Business shared_terms.status, Batch/Attempt/receipts and independent reports remain separate truths. Append an ordinary adjustment only for a substantive change; shared meaning changes still require the existing review. Missing/unverified artifacts, pending approval/application/acceptance and absent plans are progress/evidence gaps, not business unknowns. An unconfirmed proposal alone does not establish semantic ambiguity; name the actual unresolved meaning before recording explicit_unknowns. During recovery correct existing misplaced progress/evidence entries by moving their gaps into notes, without removing genuinely unresolved business unknowns or resetting unrelated expression.
progress_maintenance.after_handoff: Never overwrite a digest-bound map, source checkpoint or old report to fix stale progress. Host records discrepancies outside Judge business evidence; authorized production recovery updates its writable working copy. Emergency saving preserves current artifacts without waiting for perfect progress.
progress_maintenance.recovery: Verify checkpoint/scope/identity mapping, write reconciliation and actual candidates before updating. pending never proves unapplied; definite writes are not replayed. Fork retains neutral progress but uses new scope/identity_mapping; old receipts are source history, never new apply authority.
progress_maintenance.isolation: No hidden questions, answers or private diagnostics in the map. Same slice_id/name/scope/owner progress notifications do not reapprove scope or reopen frozen CQs. Retained R3/history artifacts keep their original meaning.

topology_decision.timing: Recorded before the first real apply; while it is missing or structurally incomplete, the independent platform MCP gate stays closed and rejects every platform call, including reads. That is expected behavior: repair the artifact from the typed reason code sent to Coordinator and wait for the next Runner re-check; do not retry platform calls.
rules: at least three options and always the three required option_ids; custom options may be appended

each options entry has exactly the two option_fields: option_id is a non-empty string, and assessment is an object whose keys are exactly the six dimensions listed above, each with a non-empty value; the dimensions are assessment keys, never an option-level dimensions container (a wrong option shape is reported as topology_schema_mismatch)

every option assesses all six dimensions with non-empty values; the dimensions are concept cohesion, relation density, reuse, permission boundary, change cadence, and cross-domain query, never table count or team count
selecting single_ontology does not waive the comparison: the full three-option, six-dimension record is still required
selected_option must be one of the listed options and rationale must be non-empty

R4.0-029 existing topology: entries are mutually exclusive {ontology_id, slice_ids} for explicit authorized existing IDs or {name, slice_ids} for new creation. New entries require allow_new_ontologies and current business topology approval; do not adopt same-name resources or precreate a first Ontology. A single_ontology selection may supply exactly one existing-ID entry. Original create topology keeps its name-based at-least-two plan contract. Each slice must be covered; slices may overlap.
create/name-only plans require at least two; an existing-ID single_ontology plan may contain one
name or ontology_id values are non-empty and unique within the plan
slice_ids is a non-empty list of distinct slice_ids of the current scenario map
every scenario-map slice belongs to at least one planned Ontology; a slice may be served by more than one planned Ontology
existing mode supports explicit ID entries and a single existing-ID entry for single_ontology; create/new-name entries still require authorization and receipt reconciliation
the artifact's field set is closed and is exactly the `fields` list; `maintainer` is contract metadata describing who maintains the artifact, never an artifact field
iri is one non-empty absolute IRI; dangling IRIs for resources not yet created are allowed
target_protection_set is existing:<id> or new:<name>
proposing_slice must be a slice of the current scenario map
format only: the decision to protect, and every execution failure, follows the existing R3.0-004 protection-set contract

execution.multi_ontology_batches: One Modeling Batch binds exactly one Ontology. A multi-Ontology topology means at least one batch per Ontology, applied by Protocol in scenario-map dependency order; dry_run then apply_atomic per batch; no cross-batch atomicity is required or provided.
execution.protection_sets: Protection sets are Project-level, may span Ontologies, and must never drive the Ontology split. Protection-set changes and ontology publication are two independent operations and are never part of the same Modeling Batch. Protecting target IRIs before creating the resources is the recommended order, not a platform constraint. If the configured native read does not expose member identities or count, do not infer the missing membership evidence. Delivery/Host may attest complete membership (each resource IRI and Ontology), allowed_grants, and observation time from canonical control-plane readback formally bound to the same Project and exact protection-set ID; this attestation supplies preprotection evidence and must be checked against the native ID/name/grants, any returned member count, and actual resource_outputs. Roles must not bypass their tool boundary to read REST endpoints or keys. Current approval, dry-run, and write gates remain required.
execution.order: Interleave viewpoint analysis within approved slice dependencies; record slice/order adjustments. Definition-before-reference is a write dependency, not a fixed semantic phase sequence.
execution.shared_changes: Reference current governed definitions. Re-review before changes (including deletion/meaning/scope). Compatible changes retain identity. Revise a definition and its affected references in one available atomic Batch. Without cross-Batch/Ontology atomicity, confirm a distinct new meaning/contract, materialize it first and switch references in safe groups while old definitions retain old meaning; otherwise defer. No same-identity version pinning or automatic compatibility inference.
